To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the photograph and the free-text components of an online dating profile both play a role in predicting the overall attractiveness of the profile; and 2) attractiveness judgments are based on a variety of profile components and are not limited to the photograph.

the attractiveness of a profile is predicted by the attractiveness and extraversion of the photo, the perceived genuineness and trustworthiness of the free-text component, and the attractiveness and extravertedness of the free-text.
the photo is the strongest predictor of overall profile attractiveness, but that the free-text component is the second strongest, and that the fixed-choice elements are unrelated to attractiveness.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how people evaluate others through their online profiles, and it provides a window into the psychology of attraction in an important social context.

the photograph is the primary determinant of perceived attractiveness, and that the free text plays an important secondary role.

the attractiveness ratings of whole profiles, photos, and free-text components are predicted by a complex set of factors, including the attractiveness of the photo, the free-text component, and a variety of other factors, including gender and age.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
users of online dating profiles do indeed use them to assess attractiveness and other qualities, as they do in offline settings.
the free text and the photo are the two most important components of the profile in predicting the attractiveness of the whole profile.
users of online dating sites have a strong preference for attractive partners and that they are willing to invest considerable time and effort in finding them.
The main takeaway from our work is that
online dating profiles are not simply a collection of individual elements, but a whole that is perceived holistically.
the attractiveness ratings of online dating profile components are predicted by different sets of qualities for men and women, and that these qualities can be used to inform profile design.
